name: Booth 2008: six circumcerebral patterns clockwise, then counter-clockwise
origin: Booth, Koren & Persinger (Laurentian University), circumcerebral "Octopus" ring; patterns from the lab's six-configuration table (Persinger, Tsang, Booth & Koren 2008)
summary: Booth, Koren & Persinger 2008 rotated the same circumcerebral patterns clockwise and counter-clockwise around the head and reported more EEG power over the left hemisphere during clockwise and over the right hemisphere during counter-clockwise rotation. This program runs the lab's six standard patterns clockwise (30 min), then the same six counter-clockwise (30 min).
notes: Booth's abstract gives no pattern list, durations, intensity or sample size: it says complex fields "with different rates of acceleration" were rotated each way; its "largest effect" with "20 ms rates of change" per solenoid sums up earlier work (Richards 2002), not a Booth result. The six patterns here are the lab's standard battery from Table 1 of Persinger, Tsang, Booth & Koren 2008 (Booth is a co-author; the paper reportedly reuses Richards 2002's six). The project could not open that paper, so the table comes secondhand and is unverified; the verified Table 1 of the Swann paper (persinger-swann-2002-table1) differs in BF2's 1-ms gap, FM2's 1-ms points and FM1's sign (+2 there, while this table reportedly prints -2). 5 min each: BF1 1 ms / 1 ms / 20 ms / +2, BF2 1 / 2 / 100 / +20, BF3 3 / 3000 / 200 / -2, FM1 1 / 1 / 20 / -2, FM2 2 / 1 / 100 / +20, FM3 3 / 3000 / 200 / -2 (point duration / gap between pattern repeats / time on coil 1 / change per coil). FM1 is played as printed. The signs are read literally, + longer and - shorter at each next coil: BF1 runs 20 to 34 ms, the +20 rows 100 to 240 ms, the 200-ms rows 200 to 186 ms and FM1 20 to 6 ms, which is what the same paper's results ("20 msec (+2 msec)") mean in the lab's later notation. Persinger & Lavallee 2010 use "+" to mean shorter, which would give 20 to 6 ms for BF1, 20 to 34 ms for FM1 and 200 to 214 ms for the 200-ms rows; the literal reading was chosen because the +20 rows cannot shorten seven times from 100 ms, Cook 1999's full turns of about 200 to 2000 ms fit it better (216 ms per turn at 20 to 34 ms, 104 ms at 20 to 6 ms), and the Koren software patent (US 6,312,376) uses the plain sign. The schedule the lab actually ran was never published. Both directions start the dwell ramp on coil 1 (Fp1); clockwise then steps to Fp2. Ring: eight coils 45 degrees apart on the 10% line, coil 1 over the left frontal region, coil 2 at the left fronto-temporal junction and coil 8 over the right prefrontal region, counter-clockwise seen from above (Persinger & Lavallee 2010): Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2, an inference since the lab names no electrode sites. The Thomas (frequency-modulated) pulse plays from its exact 849-point table; the burst-firing point values were never published, so the built-in accelerating burst stands in (230 points, 6 -> 30 Hz at 3 ms per point and three times faster at 1 ms). Intensity is not in the abstract: the lab's ring gave about 1 uT in its studies of those years (about 1 uT at the centre, Dotta & Persinger 2012; 1-5 uT inside each solenoid, Lehman 2016); Richards 2002 used 5-10 uT. Running both directions in one hour mixes direction with time in session, and the abstract does not say how Booth ordered them. persinger-octopus-plus20-cw and -ccw run a single +20-ms configuration per direction on separate days instead. Single-lab EEG result, never independently replicated. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Seated and blindfolded in a quiet, dark room (the lab used an acoustic chamber). To check the claim, record EEG over both hemispheres, for example a 20-s sample in the middle of each pattern, and compare left and right power between the two halves.
schedule: One session. For a self-test, repeat on another day and compare with a blinded sham session (the app's Blind option).
